rows.reason: Current INSPIRE Index Polygons download page states the dataset was published on 5 July 2026.
HMLR states new INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
Current INSPIRE files are downloadable by local authority.
London Borough of Lambeth is present in the current local-authority download list.
The current download page states download is subject to Open Government Licence conditions.
INSPIRE Index Polygons contain locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of HMLR's wider Index Polygons database.
Each INSPIRE Index Polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
HMLR states INSPIRE polygons show indicative position and extent, not definitive title extent.
HMLR states exact land extent for a registered title can only be identified from the individual title plan.
A single registered title can contain several separate polygons, each with a separate INSPIRE ID.
A property without an INSPIRE ID may be leasehold or another tenure omitted from this INSPIRE subset.
HMLR technical guidance states the data is captured against British National Grid.
HMLR warns BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
HMLR says an INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan information.
LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers about 99% of England.
The composite DTM spatial resolution is 1 metre.
The DTM removes surface objects to model the terrain surface.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest and best-resolution data is used.
Where data was resampled, the dataset description says bilinear interpolation was used.
The 2022 composite contains surveys undertaken from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Individual LIDAR surveys used in the composite have vertical accuracy of ±15 cm RMSE.
Dataset metadata declares EPSG:27700.
The dataset is available as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Data is presented in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Data.gov.uk metadata states the OSTN15 transformation method is used.
The Environment Agency dataset advertises a WCS endpoint for the 1m DTM.
EA guidance states WCS returns raw pixel data such as elevation.
EA states its WCS services use OGC WCS version 2.0.1.
EA guidance states WCS GeoTIFF NoData is -3.4028235e+38.
The survey-index OGC Features service lists LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents in EPSG:27700.
The DTM extents collection exposes filename, tilename, polygon_id, resolution, year, od_dtm_fn, survey dates and geometry as queryable fields.
OS Terrain 50 is an Open Data product.
OS states Terrain 50 is free to view, download and use for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
OS Terrain 50 covers Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 is published as both grid data and contour data.
Grid and contour data are supplied as 10 km by 10 km tiles.
The Terrain 50 grid uses regular 50 m post spacing.
A 10 km grid tile is represented by 200 by 200 pixels.
Grid height values are calculated from the centre of each pixel.
Height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 m.
Grid data is available in ASCII grid format.
The gridded supply includes GML alongside ASCII data.
OS Terrain 50 includes per-tile metadata in GEMINI-style XML.
OS states the online download is available with no registration required.
The national tiled supply contains 2,858 tiles.
The tiled national supply is arranged into 55 folders representing 100 km grid squares.
OS documents the full national grid supply as 157 MB compressed.
OS Terrain 50 grid data is documented as 4 m RMSE.
The current known-data-issues page states there are no live known issues.
OS Downloads API supports area=TQ filtering and returns HTTP 307 when redirect is requested and exactly one file matches.
